To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

refined quorums and high resolution timestamps are the first abstractions for asynchronous distributed BFT computing that enable designing algorithms that are optimistically fast in the absence of contention and failures (and synchronous), but degrade gracefully if failures occur (or the system is asynchronous).

(a) refined quorums are a novel abstraction for optimally resilient and optimally best-case time complexity distributed algorithms and (b) high resolution timestamps and ABsTRACT are novel abstractions for optimally resilient, optimally worst-case time complexity and optimally peak throughput distributed algorithms.

(a) refined quorum system is an abstraction for designing BFT atomic objects that are optimally robust to failures and perform fast if failures are rare and the system is synchronous; (b) high resolution timestamps are an abstraction for designing atomic objects that are robust to failures and have optimal worst-case time performance; (c) ABsTRACT is an abstraction for developing BFT-SMR that are optimally fault-tolerant and have optimal complexity, for some relevant complexity metrics.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing abstractions for asynchronous distributed systems that tolerate arbitrary failures and asynchrony, with the aim to facilitate the development of optimally resilient and optimally efficient distributed algorithms.
the development of asynchronous BFT distributed systems.
developing reusable and modular abstractions that can be used to design asynchronous BFT distributed systems that are resilient to arbitrary failures and have optimal complexity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the abstractions we propose in this thesis are useful for developing optimally resilient asynchronous BFT distributed systems that feature optimal complexity in some relevant metric.

this thesis introduces novel abstractions that facilitate the design of asynchronous BFT distributed systems, and we show how to exploit these abstractions to devise BFT solutions with the best complexity we know of, and with optimal resilience.

the thesis introduces a series of new and reusable abstractions that simplify the design of asynchronous BFT distributed systems, and in particular, algorithms that feature optimal resilience and/or complexity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our abstractions allow us to devise BFT distributed algorithms with optimal complexity in the presence of malicious behavior and asynchronicity.
this thesis proposes three new abstractions that simplify the design of optimally resilient asynchronous BFT algorithms, with optimal performance with respect the most important complexity metric.

we propose three abstractions for asynchronous distributed BFT computing, and use them to design algorithms that feature the lowest time complexity (or peak throughput), the largest resilience and the highest performance under failure-free conditions, for the most relevant BFT applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of Bft algorithms is a complex task, and it requires a number of abstractions.
abstractions can be used to design BFT algorithms that have optimal complexity, while being optimally resilient.
the design and analysis of asynchronous BFT distributed systems can be simplified by introducing adequate abstractions that capture the essence of these systems.
